content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after negative sentiment spikes; adjust downward bias by 1–2% for first 5 days if sentiment > -0.5.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ above recent high) — cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if sentiment is persistently negative (avg < -0.4 over last 5 days), model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Horizon-specific: 15–25 day forecasts show higher lag error — add 0.3–0.7% lag correction if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to catch the rebound — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day for first 3 days of sentiment shift.
